journal_lines: §aHeat up through the paws from the first step. §oSmells like dry grass and sun-hot bark.§o Scattered §lAcacia§l, but workable.
§aTwisted trunks, impossible to read the grain. Cut slow.
§aFlat light, hard shadows. The acacia stands well alone out here.
§aThe wood inside was redder than the bark. §oAcacia bleeds almost.§o Good dense timber.
§aRoots tore the ground when the trunk went over. Deep roots on these trees.
§aA vulture circled the whole time. §oPatient.§o Disappointed. Left before I did.
§aAxe got hot in the paw by midday. Kept working. §lAcacia§l worth it.
§aThorns on every branch. Took my time moving timber to the bag.
§aDead acacia still standing, bark stripped bare. Dry wood, light, easy to carry.
§aSingle long shadow from a single tree. Cut it from the long side. Good grain inside.
